metadata_history.message:
chore: prepare release v1.0.1 — banking_knowledge grading fixes (#408)

* fix(evaluate-trajs): reproduce live grading when re-scoring trajectories

Three gaps made 'tau2 evaluate-trajs' diverge from live grading:

1. It graded against the task definitions embedded in each results file,
   so criteria fixes shipped in data/ were never picked up. New
   --fresh-tasks flag reloads tasks from the current data dir by id.

2. It passed no env_kwargs, so banking_knowledge's per-task
   read_log_allowlist (runner/build.py) was never applied and
   required-read assertions silently stopped discriminating.
   compute_simulation_rewards now derives the allowlist per task.

3. Environment.set_state raised on any replayed tool-output text
   mismatch, so trajectories recorded before numeric-argument
   normalization (40ac84c) aborted on cosmetic echo drift (e.g.
   deposit_check_3847 rendering 25 vs 25.0). set_state gains a strict
   flag; re-grading passes strict=False (warn and continue, state is
   applied identically), live evaluation stays strict.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* chore: prepare v1.0.1 release docs — banking_knowledge grading and task fixes

Version bump 1.0.0 -> 1.0.1 plus CHANGELOG, RELEASE_NOTES, and GitHub
release body documenting the bundled banking_knowledge fixes (#329,
#397, #402, #403, #388) and the measured leaderboard impact
(17 submissions re-graded, +217/-0 flips). A full deterministic re-grade
under the rebased branch (including #403) reproduces every reward
exactly.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* chore: re-grade banking_knowledge leaderboard submissions under v1.0.1

17 banking_knowledge trajectory sets re-graded with the fixed
evaluate-trajs path (fresh tasks, per-task read_log_allowlist, lenient
replay). Recorded NL-assertion judgments are preserved (the 1.0.1 fixes
are all environment-side), so the re-grade is deterministic. pass^k
recomputed counting infrastructure-error sims as failed trials, matching
the original leaderboard convention. No simulation flipped from pass to
fail.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(release): document b51a6d6 as the pre-1.0.1 banking_knowledge pin

The banking_knowledge grading/task fixes bundled in 1.0.1 were merged to
main on 2026-07-14/15 without a version bump, so installs from main after
that window already behave like 1.0.1 while still reporting 1.0.0. Point
readers at b51a6d69e26f0e94a9173e2e80fe8735a8dff650 — the direct parent of
the first fix (#397) and the last commit with pre-1.0.1 behavior — as the
commit to pin for reproducing pre-release scores.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(banking_knowledge): T074 gold under-refunds Light Blue ATM fees ($8.00 → $14.50) (#412)

* fix(banking_knowledge): task_074 honors the 2-free-per-type Light Blue ATM allowance (#374)

The Light Blue Account docs (doc_..._light_blue_account_004/_006) grant
two free out-of-network and two free foreign ATM withdrawals per month,
but the gold credit for chk_ar72c5d8e3_2 honored only one of each,
under-refunding the account: $8.00 instead of the policy-faithful $14.50.
The fixture's own annotations exposed the slip, jumping from
"(SHOULD BE FREE - 1ST OF 2)" straight to "(AFTER 2 FREE)" with no 2nd
free withdrawal anywhere.

- Gold credit for the Light Blue account: $8.00 -> $14.50 (tasks.json and
  tasks/task_074.json), task notes now enumerate all 7 Light Blue fee
  errors ($17.00 overcharges minus the $2.50 missing 11/10 fee).
- db.json: the 11/06 domestic and 11/09 foreign fee descriptions are
  relabeled "(SHOULD BE FREE - 2ND OF 2)" so the fixture is consistent
  with the policy docs.
- CHANGELOG.md / RELEASE_NOTES.md / github-release-body.md: documented
  under 1.0.1 with the upward-only claim scoped to the grading-scheme
  fixes, since this changes a gold value.

Verified with `tau2 evaluate-trajs --fresh-tasks` on the sierra
trajectory sets: no trial matched the old $8.00 gold (nothing flips
down); one gemini-3-1-pro-preview trial that applied the correct $14.50
refund flips 0.0 -> 1.0.

Fixes #374

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(banking_knowledge): scrub answer-leaking annotations from Light Blue fee descriptions

The Light Blue account's atm_fee descriptions embedded the answer key the
task is supposed to test for: "(SHOULD BE FREE - 1ST OF 2)" told the agent
outright which fees were erroneous, and "(AFTER 2 FREE)" disclosed the
allowance count for the legitimate ones. The previous commit relabeled two
of these annotations; this removes all twelve, leaving plain statement-style
descriptions ("NON-RHO ATM FEE" / "FOREIGN ATM FEE") consistent with the
other three accounts, so the agent must derive the 2-free-per-type allowance
from the policy docs and the withdrawal dates.

Grading is unaffected: gold and predicted environments replay from the same
updated db.json, and no task instructions or assertions reference the old
description strings.

* fix(banking_knowledge): scrub AFTER FREE ALLOWANCE annotations from task_072/073 fixtures

Same class of leak as the Light Blue scrub: four "NON-RHO ATM FEE - AFTER
FREE ALLOWANCE" rows disclosed the bank's free-allowance bookkeeping in
agent-visible statement text. On task_072's Light Green account
(chk_538bfb9cba) the annotation appeared only on the legitimate fee while
the erroneous fee read plain "NON-RHO ATM FEE", so annotation presence alone
separated correct fees from wrong ones. On task_073's Light Green account
(chk_kj93a7b2e1_3) the label was uniform across all three fee rows, but is
scrubbed for consistency.

Description-only change: gold and predicted environments replay from the
same db.json, and no task text or assertion references these strings.

* fix(banking_knowledge): remove stray currency signs from day counts in KB docs (#414)

Mirrors sierra-research/tau2-bench-private#360 for the document files
present in this repo.

* docs: reference pre-v1.0.1 tag for reproducing pre-release grading

The last pre-fix commit (b51a6d6) is now tagged pre-v1.0.1, so the pin
instructions use the tag instead of a raw hash. Also note that grading
is identical at every earlier 2026 commit of main (verified back to
2be6916); changes in that window are simulation-side only.
